one_star_reviews.text:
I visited one of your stores  Brandy Melville Barcelona yesterday, not far from Casa Batlló. My teenage daughter was excited to discover the shop, so we spent an hour choosing clothes and eventually selected a dozen or more items that I would have happily purchased — if the sizing had been right.

Only after spending all that time did I discover that trying on clothes is not permitted in the store.

Does this really make sense in such a touristy area?

Apparently, customers are expected to take the clothes home or back to their hotel to try them on and then return to the store if they don't fit — only to receive a credit note rather than a refund.

Even more surprising, when I asked to speak to the manager, I was told that another option was to use a public or restaurant toilet to try the clothes on.

Yes, you read that correctly.

What a frustrating and completely impractical shopping experience, particularly for tourists. If you're visiting Barcelona, you may not have the convenience of a home nearby, and expecting people to take clothes back to their hotel, try them on, and then make another trip to the store is simply unreasonable.

As for making my teenage daughter try clothes on in a public toilet just to purchase cheap industrial clothing ,mind you not even if it was the highest end of brands — absolutely not.

So, despite having selected more than a dozen items and being perfectly willing to buy them, I left everything behind. An hour of shopping turned into an hour of wasted time.

It's especially disappointing because teenagers may love the clothes, but a shopping experience like this is enough to make customers walk away.

I really hope the company reconsiders this policy, particularly in a tourist destination like Barcelona. Making customers choose between buying clothes without knowing whether they fit, making a second trip to return them for a credit note, or using a public toilet as a changing room is simply not a reasonable customer experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I rented a property managed by Mariví, from Gestoría Villar and Alquileres Gala, and my experience was extremely negative from beginning to end. She was extremely punctual and demanding when it came to collecting payment, but when problems or issues arose, help was nonexistent.

During my stay, I had a major electrical problem, and despite reporting it, they completely washed their hands of the situation. I ended up having to find and pay an electrician myself to resolve a problem that should have been handled by the owner or the management company.

When I moved out, they also failed to properly inform me about the procedures related to utilities because they had put them in my name. As a result, I continued to receive bills for electricity, water, and garbage collection fees even after I had left the property. When I tried to ask for explanations and find a solution, their response was that it was "my problem," even going so far as to block me on WhatsApp and by phone.

Furthermore, they never informed me that I was responsible for personally reading the water meter. Now I'm facing a claim for approximately two years' worth of water consumption when I only lived in the property for a year and a half. I find it unacceptable that a management company that prides itself on professionalism would omit such important information and then wash its hands of the matter when the consequences arise.

My experience has been one of lack of information, lack of assistance in case of problems, and a complete lack of responsibility when issues arise. I recommend that any future tenant document absolutely everything in writing and personally review every transaction related to utilities and maintenance. In my case, I would never use their services again, nor would I recommend them to anyone.

Run away.

I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with my experience at your Baricentro store on Monday, August 10th.

First, I want to acknowledge the excellent service provided by the optometrist who performed my eye exam, who was very kind and professional. However, the management of the rest of my visit was very poor.

The manager interrupted the person assisting me several times to prioritize other customers, forcing me to switch to a different employee and repeat part of the frame selection process. At one point, I waited for more than ten minutes without being attended to, even though there were hardly any other customers in the store.

Furthermore, I found it particularly uncomfortable to feel constant pressure to choose more expensive brands, when from the beginning I had requested a simple option from your own brand.

Of the three people present, only the optometrist maintained a professional and courteous demeanor throughout.

I believe that a brand like Óptica 2000 should pay much more attention to customer service and, above all, to the organization and the treatment received from its management.

For these reasons, my experience has been decidedly negative, and I cannot recommend this establishment.

All these reviews are absolutely true, it's a shame I saw them after what happened to me. I canceled the financing within the legally established timeframe, and they told me they couldn't refund the product because it was specially ordered for me. The saleswoman didn't even come to help us when we went to pick it up. Honestly, paying for it is the least of my worries; what I find disrespectful is that they can't resolve anything like this. Completely unprofessional, completely lacking in empathy. They were even whispering amongst themselves because I requested a formal complaint.

In short, zero professionalism.

My advice: find a tutorial on YouTube, buy the materials on Amazon, and save yourself €100! 👍

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm writing from San Vicente del Raspeig. I have to say that a year later I still haven't managed to get my license, because I think they don't handle the practical driving lessons very well. I'm continuing with them because I thought I'd have a similar or even better experience with the theory test and their "pass" method. But the reality is quite different, especially with the practical part. Unfortunately, having to wait two months after passing the theory test to be able to do practical driving lessons isn't what you expect. Then, when you finally get something... you have to keep waiting for them to open up regular slots. But if you can't stand waiting, don't risk it. They lose some of their value here. At first, I was really eager to get my practical driving test. There weren't that many hours available, so I averaged about 20. Without further success, due to the situation I've described. I went back and waited another two months. I've started again with another 36 hours. But to my surprise... I'll probably have to wait another two months. It's a real shame, because the administration seems good. It would be even better if they actually allowed continuity for someone who's already put in over 50 hours. But because of this intermittent schedule, it's impossible. I have a baby with a disability and who is dependent on me. I've mentioned this. I've requested a change of instructor even though Professor Ramon is very good. But my goal is to have continuity, even though I know it's something I struggle with. And if I still have all these obstacles, it seems like a lost cause. There's a lot of demand and a limited and inefficient supply. I'll keep my fingers crossed because, looking at the September 2026 calendar (since there are two weeks of vacation now), I'll only have six classes and I'll almost certainly have to wait until October. Seriously...? This is a serious problem that you should consider if you're looking for continuous availability for practical classes so you don't waste so much time. The method has a 5 rating, but with the practical sessions, that rating isn't possible. 😿
Price assessment
Overpriced
Services
Private lessons

one_star_reviews.text: I'd been going to this shop for months. I'd left some gold items there, and in the last few months, I'd gone twice to have silver pieces appraised. The last time, the price was 19 cents per gram (she herself told us it wasn't very high at the time), so we decided to leave them at home, keep looking for more pieces, and wait. We weren't even going to buy from other places, since this woman seemed to be doing a good job, and if the price was right, we planned to leave everything there and not complicate things. Today I went with more pieces, and the service was completely different. She looked at them, offered me a price with very little communication (50 cents per gram, more than double the previous price), and told me that if I hadn't left the previous pieces and hadn't left these ones, she'd get in trouble "from above" if she appraised a lot of pieces and then we didn't leave them there. With today's price per pound, I would have gone to drop off today's and yesterday's orders, but with the service I received, I join the other reviews and recommend not going.

one_star_reviews.text:
A disgrace. We booked an apartment with this company whose advertisement clearly showed photos of two bathrooms, a feature that is part of the information provided at the time of booking and is binding. However, when we arrived, we found that the apartment only had one. They were perfectly aware that the advertisement did not correspond to reality.

We complained immediately, and instead of offering us a suitable relocation solution, as required by law, the only response we received was a refund and that we had to vacate the accommodation. All of this in the middle of August, peak season, with very high tourist occupancy, and while traveling with three children.

Given their inability to provide us with accommodation under the agreed-upon conditions, we requested that they offer us an alternative with equivalent or superior features, as is appropriate in these situations. They refused.

To make matters worse, someone from the agency even called the Civil Guard to try to evict us, claiming we were "squatting" and making noise, despite having a confirmed reservation, having legally entered the accommodation, and having three babies sleeping inside. Obviously, the officers ignored the claims and did not carry out the eviction.

In the end, we had to find other accommodation on our own, thankfully much better, although also more expensive. Given this company's behavior, we had no choice but to file a formal complaint with the Consumer Protection Agency.

After having laminate flooring installed in my home, the material has lifted and warped across the entire surface due to poor workmanship. Despite notifying them immediately to find a solution, the company has ignored my complaints. The installation was completed last January, and as of today, August 24th, they have not resolved the problem and are not answering calls or WhatsApp messages. Deplorable after-sales service. Absolute lack of responsibility and professionalism. Beware of them; don't trust their good rating, it seems very suspicious to me, probably from friends or purchased reviews. And be careful with the invoices they issue; they are pro forma invoices, not valid for tax purposes, which is suspicious because they allegedly charge VAT but don't declare it.

I have recorded videos, but I think it only allows me to post photos, and the warping isn't visible in the photos. Anyway, I'm posting some photos of the baseboards where the poor quality of the work is already apparent.

one_star_reviews.text:
Everything I'm about to say is true, and here's how it works:

I had a colovaginoplasty with them. Of course, it was a public tender with the Andalusian Health Service (SAS), and the treatment of those of us who had it done through the public healthcare system is appalling. They have a phone number and email address specifically for people who haven't paid €20,000 for this type of surgery. I had my colovaginoplasty on May 8th at the Vithas Xanit Hospital in Benalmádena, where IM GENDER was the team in charge of these surgeries. The treatment of those of us who had this type of surgery by the clinic has been degrading. You write to their corporate WhatsApp number and they answer you in a week, 10 days, or sometimes not at all. Women like me are left unprotected. In my case, there are noticeable asymmetries even though 80% of the swelling has gone down, if not all of it. Another important point is that the appointments with the doctor are video calls with a person. The call (DR-ALEMAN) or that's his ID in the video calls, video calls of course where you can't feel or touch anything necessary to check that everything is correct since he doesn't even ask you to show him the area. Video calls for 3, 6, and 12 months, and if you really want them to examine you properly, you have to beg them. I suppose you don't receive the same treatment when you pay 20,000 or 25,000 for this surgery as when you go through the public system and it's free. After several attempts to get proper care for myself and all the other women who have had the same surgery, my only option now is to file a complaint.

one_star_reviews.text: Unpresentable, they're only after easy money and have little integrity.

I went to Esmeralda seeking professional help, and my experience has been deeply disappointing, debilitating, and, in my opinion, harmful.

The worst part was feeling my perceptions invalidated and my boundaries constantly questioned. On occasion, when I managed to defend myself against disrespect within my family, instead of validating my progress, she lectured me about 'assertiveness' and respect, making me feel guilty for protecting myself. If I explained that a friend was treating me badly and showed her the messages with the boundaries I wanted to set, she would edit the texts to make them sound much more submissive and compliant. She even went so far as to justify this person's continuous disrespect (like ignoring me for days or telling me I had a time limit in the middle of a get-together) by comparing it to her own personal experience: she argued that she also routinely took a long time to reply to her friends, that relationships aren't perfect, and that if I set boundaries "at the slightest provocation," she personally would find it hard to be my friend.

On a technical level, I felt incredibly rigid. During the EMDR session, I explained that the eye movements were overwhelming me and suggested standard alternatives like tapping or auditory stimulation. Although she verbally offered other options, she did so in a way that made me feel mentally cornered into choosing her method, insisting that the eye movements provided more evidence. I expected a genuine adaptation to my needs, not to feel pressured to continue with the same method. She also linked my proactivity to a "need for control" and to "going too fast," even warning me of a possible serious relapse, when what I was seeking was greater efficiency, not speed. I tried to resolve this issue via WhatsApp, but she insisted on leaving it for an in-person consultation. However, once there, she accused me of wasting time that should be used for "healing," and when I reminded her that I had tried to resolve it via text message, she reproached me, saying it wasn't the appropriate channel. He cornered me in a contradiction that made me cry with helplessness, to which he simply repeated a cold, robotic "I'm here," which I found deeply uncomfortable and retraumatizing.

The lack of administrative professionalism culminated in my decision to leave. After a session, I asked him via WhatsApp a question about payment for the following sessions. He said he would look into it the following week. Less than 48 hours before the appointment, I reminded him of the question with a simple '?', and he only replied with a period ('.'), so I had to explain and justify my question again to get a real answer.

At the end of the therapy, he obstructed me from receiving my digital medical record, trying to force me to do it in person, citing confidentiality reasons. He only agreed to send me the document when I demanded my rights, invoking Article 15 of the GDPR and the Patient Autonomy Act (Article 18 of Law 41/2002). After reviewing my medical record, I found that she omitted the technical issues that occurred during the consultation and included a diagnosis that, in my opinion, was completely inconsistent with the symptoms described in the document itself.

I would not recommend this professional to anyone seeking a safe space, genuine empathy, and clinical adaptability.

UPDATE: I stand by my assessment in full. I find it particularly significant that, in response to a review where I explained that I felt my boundaries were being challenged, the reply again publicly lectured me about how "healthy relationships" should function and insisted on respecting other people's time and needs. She also presented what happened as a difference in "perception" or context, without acknowledging any specific error in her intervention. I also retain my recollection of the expressions I described, including the reference to "laziness." The response itself also confirms that an in-person collection of my medical history was initially proposed.

So, I made a trip for nothing. On Wednesday of that same week, I ordered my contact lenses and a new pair of glasses. One of the women who works there asked if I wanted to pick up the contact lenses that same day, and I said no, I would take everything together. A week passed and they didn't call me, so I went to ask when I could pick everything up, and it turned out they only had the glasses. I don't understand how it's possible that the day I placed the order, my glasses were missing, and they offered to deliver the contact lenses that same day. A week later, my contact lenses are missing, especially after I told them I was going to be traveling, which isn't their problem. It's very strange that I can't get my contact lenses on time now, when the day I placed the order, a week and two days ago, they said I could pick up the lenses that same day. To make matters worse, I explained to one of the women that a colleague told me I could pick up the lenses that day, and she says that's impossible. Why would I lie about something like this?

one_star_reviews.text: Horrible. They pressure you and put you in situations where they force you to buy treatments and packages you don't need, and when you ask for a refund because they refuse to give you an appointment on the days you book, they don't give you one either. It's a scam. The saleswoman, Lidia, was very unprofessional, tactless, and extremely unfriendly.

My experience with Dorsia Sant Andreu has been very negative due to their handling of a cancellation and refund. I formally requested the cancellation of a treatment within the 30-day period stipulated in my contract. Since then, I have sent emails, WhatsApp messages, made several calls, and visited the clinic in person on several occasions. They confirmed receipt of my request and promised to call me back, but that call never came. Subsequently, I was verbally informed that, "as per protocol," they did not issue refunds and that the money could be used as credit for other treatments, even though my contract includes reimbursement for services not provided within the specified timeframe. I was also told that expenses would be deducted, including an operating room reservation fee, but I am still waiting for a written breakdown and the corresponding receipts. Furthermore, the procedure was already scheduled, and pre-operative tests had been performed, yet I had not even had a consultation with the surgeon who was going to perform the operation. My main complaint is the lack of response, follow-up, and clarity in the process. To this day, I am still waiting for a formal response and the requested breakdown.

Very unprofessional. Very dishonest advice, just trying to make a sale. My daughter was pressured by the consultant Lydia into signing up for an expensive treatment without being properly informed. Don't trust her.

AWFUL! The beauty consultant pressured me into paying for a treatment and lied to me to avoid canceling it, even though my rights as a customer allowed me to do so.

The staff wouldn't answer my calls or help me with my questions.

The staff has very little moral compass; they're more focused on making a sale than helping others.

We had been waiting a month for a test. When we arrived, the receptionist (a blonde woman) treated us very rudely. When we complained about her attitude, she took it personally and said she couldn't find my husband's file, saying this in a mocking tone. We decided to go up to the third floor where the MRI scans are done, and there they told us that the file did exist, but there must have been a mistake since the appointment wasn't registered. We have to say, this woman resolved the problem and sent us to Portugalete, which was far away, but at least she gave us an appointment.

We regret this person's behavior, how badly she treated us, her denial that the information was even there, and on top of that, her failure to honor the appointment we already had, forcing us to go all the way to Portugalete. A very bad experience; I absolutely do not recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
Appalling service from the staff at the counter on pick up. I was essentially bullied as they attempted to convince me to pay an additional non refundable €500 for damage protection. They repeatedly denied that I was able to rent the car without this, even though I repeatedly explained that I had travel insurance that covered this and European breakdown cover. Ultimately, they only backed down on this when I asked my husband to come into the office. The sexism is shocking.

The car that I was provided had scratches to the wing mirror and along the drivers side. I suspect that they will have charged someone for the repair of this but simply pocketed the money instead of fixing it.

There was also no screen wash in the vehicle which would suggest that basic checks are not done between rentals.

I am thoroughly disappointed with my experience and will not be renting with OK mobility again.

A further note - the staff initially offered me a larger car. They phrased this as though it was complementary but later tried to make me pay more for it. Again, just pushy and sneaky sales practices.

We specifically booked an SUV because we needed the extra space, but the vehicle we were given was extremely small and did not meet what we had booked or expected.

We were also very unhappy with the customer service when returning the car. The member of staff was rude and unhelpful, which made an already disappointing experience worse.

Most importantly, we were not informed until the day we landed and went to collect the car that the basic insurance required a deposit of just under €2,000. We were therefore left with little choice but to pay an additional €120 for the better insurance, which reduced the deposit to €600. This should have been made clear when booking, not at the collection desk.

Overall, I am very disappointed with the service and would not recommend using your company.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Raquel wasn't good. I went to therapy with her a few years ago, and there were several situations that made me feel uncomfortable and which, with hindsight and after working with other professionals, I consider completely inappropriate.

Sometimes, when I told her about specific things that were worrying me, she would ask questions that I perceived as more out of personal curiosity than as part of the therapy, such as wanting to see photos of the brands I worked with, asking for my Instagram account, or asking for personal details that didn't seem relevant to what we were discussing.

She even told me to stop taking a prescribed medication, something that later caused me considerable concern and that my psychiatrist considered completely unreasonable. Personally, I felt more judged than supported, which is why I stopped going.

I didn't write a review at the time, but after having other therapeutic experiences, I've decided to share mine so that it can serve as a reference for others.

one_star_reviews.text:
Yesterday, during the novena to Our Lady of Sales, I experienced something that still hurts.

The moment came to hold hands. The person next to me looked at me as if I were contaminated, as if touching me was something to be avoided.

And the two seats next to me remained empty. As if I were a bitch.

Can this really happen in the house of God?

I was dressed simply. I wasn't wearing a formal suit, nor did I belong to any privileged group. But I carried what was most important: my faith, my respect, and the same desire to celebrate our patron saint as anyone else.

I don't want a Church where clothes, money, or social standing determine who deserves respect and who doesn't.

I want a Church where we are all equal. Where no one is excluded. Where no one is looked down upon. Where an outstretched hand finds another hand, and not a look of contempt.

Because when we stand before God, there are no rich or poor, elegant or simple, privileged or excluded. There are people. There are brothers and sisters.

And if we have forgotten that, perhaps it is time to ask ourselves what kind of community we are building.

The house of God must have its doors open to all, but also its heart.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Triquos has been completely negative, not at all recommended, insulting, and unprofessional. They're only motivated by money; if you don't have your credit card out front, they won't tell you if your problem has a solution or not.
They have no shame, writing in my consultation report that I'm mentally deficient and have body image dysphoria. They also have no shame in including what was said during the consultation, which is completely inappropriate. In a previous consultation with Dr. Arencibia, but for my hair, he mentioned that if I wanted, I could have an eyebrow transplant to cover a scar on my eyebrow from a nerve injury.
When I returned, this time with Dr. Guerrero, she told me in two minutes that it couldn't be done. I couldn't believe it; I felt ripped off. €110 for a two-minute consultation, same problem, and a different opinion? Did she really enjoy taking my money? I'm sure she did. I made my anger known.

So what was the problem? That the graft on the scar wasn't going to take well, or that I'm crazy?

I wanted to share my experience so you can see what kind of person I'm talking about. There's spite in the report I received from the doctor. She knows I can't submit that report, that's why she did it the way she did.

This frame is practically touching the slats, just two centimeters away, and it causes a deformity in my back. In some areas, the mattress sinks correctly, while in others it doesn't, creating a very awkward, mountain-like posture. This can worsen my health. If you have back problems, this product could make them worse.

The manufacturer even came to see it, and what's more, they sent someone with multiple back problems, ailments, saying they were about to have surgery, that they had a history of back issues, that they used a respirator—stories that had nothing to do with the product—trying to elicit sympathy. This way, you can't convince anyone; it's not a good technique.

I find it completely absurd and pathetic. Look at other stores besides Sueños Descans, because honestly, at Sueños Descans, they don't know much about the subject. Other stores know more than Sueños Descans.

The company manager and Sueños Descans in general have greatly disappointed me. And to top it all off, the manager of this company, Sueños Descans, called me fat before even trying to address the problem indirectly.

Terrible accommodation. The website doesn't specify that not all apartments have balconies. On the day of arrival, they sent us a WhatsApp message informing us that our apartment was on the ground floor. We went to complain, and the response was that they couldn't do anything and explained that they give priority for balconies to those who book through Booking.com. We doubt they comply with fire safety regulations; there's no fire extinguisher or evacuation plan, although if there were one, it would be a death trap since, as I said, there isn't a single window accessible from the street. A disgrace.

The receptionist offered us the options of being relocated to a different place each night, two by two, or a refund and leaving. They should warn guests about the construction, but of course, money talks.

⚠️IT'S A SCAM. BEWARE OF MASTERD.

In my experience, it's a scam. They sell you the course as if it were the best training available, promising support, instructors, and an excellent certificate. But after signing up, the reality is completely different.

The support is practically nonexistent, the messages with the instructors are ineffective, and the videos are mediocre. You pay an exorbitant amount to basically receive videos and be told to study on your own.

Furthermore, they assured me over the phone that the certificate would be excellent, and I later discovered that it has no official academic validity.

The most worrying thing is that they tell you many things over the phone and not in writing. Therefore, if you are thinking of signing up, record the calls and ask for absolutely everything in writing before signing.

In my case, I feel like they sold me something that doesn't match what I actually received, and now, on top of that, they are still demanding payment.

Be extremely careful before signing up with MasterD. Do your research.

You should investigate; it seems more people end up scammed than satisfied.

I went to the store at 8:31 PM to drop off a package. The store was still open, and to my surprise, the saleswoman told me that package drop-off and pick-up only take place until 8:30 PM because after that time she has to attend to other tasks.

I find it completely unreasonable that they would refuse to accept a package for just one minute, especially when the store is still open and the process could have been completed in a matter of seconds.

I understand that they might have specific hours for this service, but if so, it should be clearly indicated to prevent customers from going there only to encounter this situation.

Furthermore, the way she treated me was quite unpleasant and lacked empathy. Of course, I won't be going back, and I will advise everyone I know not to.

one_star_reviews.text:
I entered the shop with my two daughters, aged four and ten. They were checking a toy. The eldest daughter removed a sticker from the toy to demonstrate its workings to her younger sister. She then placed it back the toy with  the sticker . Suddenly, a seller approached her rudely, demanding payment and accusing her of miss using the toys . I was just three steps  away, getting some sunscreen, and returned to pay when I found my daughter crying.

Firstly, let’s consider the context. This is a shop in the airport where children come to see, and maybe if something gets their attention to buy  a  toy. She didn’t break anything; she didn’t remove it from a package, she did not brake it and she wasn’t alone for more than five minutes. Couldn’t the seller have waited a moment and approached me to explain what was happening? Instead, it was easier to come and make a child cry and accuse me of not educating my daughter properly. Seriously?  Please lady  change jobs because we’re customers with children in the airport’s kids’ section, and they didn’t exhibit inappropriate behaviour.

Please avoid coming to the duty-free shop, El Merecido. Give your money to someone else.

To the lady who intervened and said nothing happened:

Yes, nothing happened. I agree that nothing happened that I couldn’t have apologised for, paid for the toy, or adhered to the shop’s policy. But why did it happen? What happened is a bad experience and unnecessary use of power from an adult to a children…

To the male manager or colleague that talked to my daughter and tried to calm her …. thanks for your attention to us and kindness….

Very bad experience with Marlex

I've been having problems receiving my salary for two months. First, they told me they were going to deduct almost €700 because I supposedly hadn't completed the required hours. After waiting a month, they only deposited half of it, and when I called, they told me it was a mistake.

Now they're telling me I have to wait another month because the payday has already passed. This month, the same thing is happening again: I've been waiting for my salary for over a week, and when I call to ask, they tell me they're working on it and will let me know when they have an answer.

I find this situation very unprofessional, because we're talking about someone's salary and money they need for their expenses. I understand that mistakes can happen, but after so many problems and so much waiting, I think they should resolve this much more quickly and provide a clear explanation.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience at Booknovias has been, honestly, one of the most disappointing experiences I've ever had regarding something as important and special as choosing my wedding dress.

My mother and I went to the store after speaking with the owner on the phone. She explained that she was closing down and that I should hurry to make an appointment because she was receiving many bookings. We went to the store that same morning.

From the very first moment, I explained that my favorite designer was Rosa Clará. She started showing me dresses that, according to her, were from Pronovias and Rosa Clará. I tried on three, and I particularly liked one of them. She assured me it was a Rosa Clará dress.

My mother insisted that I try on a few more before deciding, but she refused, so we finally left convinced, and I made the purchase for €1,200, even though we had been told the dress was worth €1,500.

Imagine my surprise when I got home and couldn't find the dress on the Rosa Clará website. When I took the dress out of its garment bag, I discovered the label said Adriana Alier, not Rosa Clará.

But the problem didn't end there. Upon closer inspection of the dress in good light, I saw that the entire train was stained and there was a tear along one side.

After paying €1,200 for a wedding dress, I believe it's perfectly reasonable to expect it to be delivered in perfect condition and that the information provided about it is accurate.

Furthermore, the dress's garment bag broke its zipper after only opening it twice.

The first thing I did was try to contact the owner. I'd only been home for two hours and wanted to call her personally to explain what had happened and, above all, to find a solution calmly and politely. She didn't answer her phone and told me via WhatsApp that she couldn't speak to me. Finally, my mother managed to speak to her from a number she didn't have saved.

We explained the situation politely, and at no point did we intend to create any conflict. We simply wanted a solution. However, the conversation turned very unpleasant because we were accused of mistreating her, something I completely disagree with and consider unfair after how we tried to handle the situation.

I even suggested going to the store and returning the dress, as I wasn't happy with the purchase, and no solution was offered.

And I want to clarify something: if I had received a dress in perfect condition, with the correct information, and had been treated appropriately when a problem arose, this review probably wouldn't even exist. What led me to write it is the series of events and, especially, the lack of a solution when I tried to resolve it.

Luckily, I later decided to go to Zaragoza, where my experience was completely different. There, I was treated from the very first moment with professionalism, kindness, and attention that I greatly appreciated after everything that had happened. They listened to me, advised me, and helped me rediscover the joy in something that should have been beautiful from the start.

And it was there that I finally found MY wedding dress and was able to have the experience I truly hoped for: feeling excited, supported, and confident in such an important decision.

That's why I want to end by saying that I am incredibly grateful to the professionals in Zaragoza who managed to turn around an experience that had started so badly and allow me to finally enjoy choosing my dress.

My advice to any bride considering buying from Booknovias is to carefully check the brand, the style, the label, and the condition of the dress before making any payment. For me, trust and the service I received are fundamental in such a special purchase, and in this case, unfortunately, my experience fell short.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this lawyer has been very disappointing, and I would not hire her services again.

From the beginning, I asked to know how much it would cost to handle my declaration of heirs and requested a quote before proceeding. I didn't receive a clear quote or a breakdown of the fees beforehand.

I gave her €300 for her services and for accompanying me, but when I later specifically asked what that €300 was for, I didn't get a clear explanation.

In addition, there were €380 for notary fees, so I ended up paying €680 related to the declaration of heirs.

What I consider especially serious is the lack of prior information. When I asked how much the notary fees might cost, first she said it apparently wouldn't exceed €500, then that it might be that amount, and finally she literally told me, "If we don't even know how much it is, it might even be less than €300." In the end, it was €380.

My problem isn't that a notary charges €380, because I fully understand that the notary's fees aren't set by the lawyer. My problem is that I started the whole process without a clear understanding of what the lawyer was charging me, what services were included, what exactly the €300 I paid covered, and what additional expenses I would have to pay.

When I hire a legal professional, I expect precisely the opposite: transparency, clear information, and security before handing over any money or starting any proceedings. I don't want to have to keep asking what I've paid or discovering the costs as the process unfolds.

Once I received the declaration, I personally expressed my disappointment and decided to end the professional relationship and not entrust her with any further matters.

I'm publishing this review to share my personal and documented experience, and so that others know that if they decide to hire her services, I recommend requesting a detailed written estimate, outlining what services are included, the professional fees, and what external expenses will need to be paid separately, before paying anything at all.

In my case, the lack of transparency and economic communication has been enough for me not to return and not to recommend their services.

one_star_reviews.text: Three months ago, I asked the clinic if they specialized in TMJ physiotherapy, and they said yes. I went to the appointment and asked the same question again, and they confirmed it. I explained my problem to the physiotherapist who saw me (a displaced jaw disc that was causing me considerable pain), and he said that it could sometimes be corrected with physiotherapy. I agreed to the treatment, but it was quite painful, and he gave my jaw two sharp jerks. From that day on, I started having tinnitus. I thought it was temporary and would go away, but to this day, I still have it, and it's worse than the pain I had when I went. I asked if I could come back from the session I had, and they told me it's very likely, and that the technique of sharp jaw jerks is no longer used because it's too aggressive. I'm sharing all of this here so that this technique isn't used again and so that no one else has to go through what I did, because having tinnitus is quite difficult. I can't talk about other treatments because I've only gone once for what I've described.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving one star because I can't give less. I'm sharing my experience so there's a record and people know what kind of lawyers work for this company.
I had an accident on March 23rd. It was completely through no fault of mine; a car crashed into the back of mine. My insurance company is Mutual, and they work with these lawyers. On March 31st, a lawyer from this company contacted me to say she would be handling my claim and that we would be in touch. From that date until June, nobody said anything to me, nobody called me—neither the insurance company nor the lawyers; they all disappeared. Because of my studies, I couldn't take action sooner, and in June I decided to do something since they weren't doing anything. I finally contacted both the insurance company and the lawyers, but they just kept passing the buck. To my surprise, the lawyer was no longer with the company, but nobody contacted me during all this time to discuss anything. They tell me the expert has already submitted the report to the other party's insurance company, but it's not finalized, so that's what they're waiting for. I have to take action to speed things up, and in July I decided to fix the car myself since neither the assigned lawyer nor the insurance company is doing anything. In fact, I think the lawyer is avoiding talking to me. To this day, I'm still waiting to receive the compensation. It's been three weeks since I sent all the documentation to the lawyer, and today I called, and they first told me she wasn't there or who knows where she is, and then that the documentation still hasn't been passed on to the other party. This is unbelievable! What have they done in these three weeks, I wonder? It's been almost six months, I've been without a car for five, and I wonder how much longer it will be before I get my money. I've been incredibly patient already, and it looks like I still have a long way to go... They're both unprofessional, both Mutua Madrileña and Letra2. In the end, I'm going to have to hire a private lawyer so they'll finally get moving! What a shame!!

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving one star for the luggage storage service offered by this fruit shop in collaboration with Radical Storage.

What's advertised on the app doesn't match what you find upon arrival. You pay in advance and only then are you told the location, which in this case turned out to be this fruit shop.

Secure lockers? None. They simply collect your bags and put them in a storage area that the customer can't access. There are no lockers, no visible security system, and no sense that your luggage is actually protected.

Furthermore, the app allowed reservations until 3:00 PM, while the fruit shop closed at 2:30 PM. This is clearly contradictory information that should be clearly stated before payment.

Overall, the experience conveys very little transparency and security. I understand that some of the information depends on Radical Storage, but as an establishment offering this service, they should clearly state the conditions and guarantee proper luggage handling.

I would not use this service at this establishment again and I do not recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text:
I absolutely do not recommend this care home. Our experience has been horrific and has caused us enormous concern for the care of our elderly relatives.

Our family member left the care home after a significant decline, with dehydration, a weight loss of approximately 10 kg, and a substantial loss of muscle mass, to the point of being medically assessed as suffering from protein-energy malnutrition after being admitted to the hospital's emergency room.

The most worrying aspect is that the care home's own doctor didn't seem to be aware of the extent of her decline or the weight loss she had suffered. But the problem wasn't just the lack of communication with the family. We also discovered that she was being medicated with drugs that had a sedative effect, to the point of leaving her practically asleep or "half-drugged," without the family having been informed beforehand or receiving a clear explanation of the reason for this medication. In an elderly person with Alzheimer's, this seems especially serious to us, as they need to be able to eat, drink, communicate, and remain minimally active.

Furthermore, there is something as basic as hydration. A person with Alzheimer's may not ask for water or be able to express thirst, so it's impossible to rely on the resident to request a drink. However, in our experience, there was no adequate monitoring of fluid intake, with the consequences we subsequently witnessed.

During this period, there were also dehydration problems, infections, falls, and significant overall decline, requiring several medical evaluations.

Added to all this is something we find particularly concerning: the residence lacks adequate air conditioning, even in the common areas, which we consider completely unacceptable for elderly people, especially those who are vulnerable during the warmer months.

Our impression was one of zero control, zero monitoring, and utterly inadequate communication with the family.

A care home should not simply house our elderly relatives. There must be genuine monitoring of nutrition, hydration, weight, medication, drowsiness levels, falls, and changes in health status, along with clear communication with the family when anything changes.

Our experience has been disastrous, and we absolutely do not recommend this residence. Before entrusting the care of a family member there, we recommend that any family ask in detail how they monitor hydration, nutrition, weight loss, medication, alertness, infections, and the temperature conditions of the facilities.

one_star_reviews.text:
Appalling management and a complete lack of empathy!

From the first contact, I explained my situation in detail and specifically asked if the consultation was covered by my Sanitas insurance. They assured me without hesitation that it was. I communicated with them for an entire week, always with the same customer service representative, to whom I sent my medical tests and reports to prepare for the appointment.

However, to my surprise, just 24 hours before the appointment, when they already had my complete medical history, they called to tell me that they ultimately wouldn't cover it because they considered it a "second opinion," and that the fee would be €500 privately. The only justification they gave me was "it's company policy."

Playing with someone's time and vulnerability in the midst of cancer treatment like this is intolerably unethical and unprofessional. They have demonstrated a purely commercial and money-driven approach, with zero sensitivity towards the patient. Completely disappointing; I wouldn't recommend them to anyone!

one_star_reviews.text: A con artist. That's the word. I went in for terrible back pain, and he started telling me that one of my legs was shorter than the other. He tried to make me believe, like I was an idiot, that the problem was coming from somewhere else. He pressed hard under my left collarbone and more lightly on the right to make me think that was the source of the problem. As if I couldn't tell the difference in pressure on the muscle. When he finished (and I couldn't even bend my back), he told me to put my socks on and take them off, insisting I do it as if he'd performed a miracle on my back, which obviously hadn't happened. I wasn't expecting to leave pain-free, not by a long shot, but I also wasn't expecting to be taken for a ride. Just walking in and seeing that he had no qualifications and a place that looked like something out of an '80s gangster movie, I should have run for the hills yesterday. He charged me €54. I've never felt so ripped off in my life.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this lawyer has been very negative due to a complete lack of communication, passivity, and unprofessional handling of my case.

After an initial phone consultation in which I was given a quote of €60, I emailed her the documents she had requested (for the record). When she didn't respond, and given the urgency of my situation, I had to go to her office in person to make sure she received them in hard copy, as I wasn't sure if it was exactly the documentation she had requested, as I had indicated in the emails (also for the record). The secretary greeted me in the lobby, and then Mara—whom the secretary had called—came out to greet me, explaining the delay by saying she was very busy. That same day, she scheduled an appointment for me a week later.

At that appointment, I paid her the €60. I asked for an invoice, but she told me that with VAT it would come to around 70 euros, that she worked with a "receipt" (which was the same thing), and that this amount would be deducted later when I formalized the engagement letter.

Since the engagement letter hadn't arrived, after a few days I called her. She answered the phone saying she'd been in court all morning, and it seems she finally got going, because she sent me the engagement letter shortly after: a very basic and inadequate document. She also refused to let me speak with the civil servant I'd requested to obtain a certificate (meaning I had to go myself) and offered no further explanation. Given the complete lack of explanation, I started investigating on my own and sent her a very detailed email to both of her email addresses with several points and suggestions on how we could approach the case. I never received a reply to that email.

After another week or so without her answering my messages, I tried to contact her by text message and voice call (she doesn't have WhatsApp). Seeing that it was impossible to contact her, I sent her a final email terminating our attorney-client relationship and requesting the return of my policy and documentation. It was then that she called me (though I couldn't answer) and I read her reply in which she excused herself by saying she had been away all week and that my emails had gone to her spam folder.

This was unacceptable and a complete abandonment of the process. I'm sharing this so people know how it works and to remind them of something fundamental that many of us are unaware of: professionals have an obligation to inform clients in advance if they will charge for a consultation or for reviewing documents. Furthermore, the engagement letter is a preliminary estimate that must be provided and reviewed free of charge to ensure agreement before signing or paying anything, and you should never pay anything blindly or in advance without proper explanation. Get informed and ask questions before proceeding.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience was very disappointing. About a year ago, I went to a consultation with my mother after traveling some 400 km. The appointment was very brief: about 10 minutes with me and another 10 with my mother. He told my mother to see a psychologist.

What affected me most was that, while we were paying, the professional left without saying goodbye or explaining anything because he was in a hurry. We felt deeply dismissed and lacked empathy.

I didn't express this at the time because I was feeling unwell and didn't have the strength to defend myself. A year later, when I was able to, I wrote to him directly to explain how I experienced that situation. I haven't received any response or apology.

For me, especially when it comes to mental health, human interaction and empathy are just as important as professional care.

one_star_reviews.text:
A company where my experience left me with the feeling that people don't matter much.

When I started as a Production Technician, I had to relocate quickly from Guadalajara to Zaragoza, which involved moving and assuming all the expenses and commitments that came with the move. I was fully committed to the position and the company from the very beginning.

During the selection process and the various interviews, I wasn't informed of any specific physical requirements for the job.

From my first days on the job, I realized that my height (1.55 m) made the work difficult, as it involves handling radioactive material in a lead-lined chamber where it's necessary to reach and see certain areas to perform some tasks correctly. This difficulty was known and even mentioned by colleagues and supervisors. Although I reported the problem several times and suggested possible solutions, such as having a suitable support to reach and see the work areas correctly, no adjustments were made. Even so, I did everything I could to learn and adapt to the existing conditions.

My joining the company coincided with a period of high employee turnover, creating significant pressure to learn quickly. There were discrepancies between the tasks new employees were theoretically capable of performing and the practical tasks we needed to complete to learn the job properly. Direct supervision on the factory floor was limited, and much of the learning depended on my colleagues.

Another aspect I consider particularly important is the lack of feedback during my training period. During those months, I received no clear evaluation of my progress, nor was I given specific information about which aspects of my performance I needed to improve, which expectations I wasn't meeting, or if there was any risk of not passing the probationary period. Therefore, I didn't have the opportunity to know in advance if my performance was being considered insufficient or to correct any mistakes I might be making.

My relationship with the team was positive, and I believe I worked well with my colleagues. In fact, after I left, several colleagues stayed in touch, and one of them even helped me later to find new job opportunities. This contrasts with the possibility that there was an integration or attitude problem on my part.

What I consider particularly serious was the way the employment relationship ended. After having made the effort to relocate and commit to a position where I later discovered there was a significant physical challenge for me, I was summoned and told that I had not passed the probationary period, the reason given being that my learning was somewhat slower. All of this was done without any prior feedback that would have allowed me to understand this assessment and without any attempt to accommodate the difficulty I had reported.

The notification of my failure to pass the probationary period was delivered during a night shift, after I had gone to the plant specifically to continue my workday. The company is also located about 50 km from Zaragoza, so the commute was considerable. In my experience, the way the decision was communicated seemed insensitive, especially considering that I had not previously received clear feedback on my performance.

Furthermore, during my time in the role, operators could work up to two consecutive weeks on the night shift, which I personally found particularly demanding.

In short, I believe my experience reflects significant problems with planning, selection, prior information, onboarding, training, supervision, and communication.

A very, very bad experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it one star because Google's system doesn't allow zero. If you want to save time on medical consultations, this is the clinic for you: they don't need to see you in person, use a trichoscope, or examine the density of your donor area. They only need a couple of photos via WhatsApp to give you a definitive diagnosis by email and send you on your way in two minutes. They don't even call to deliver the bad news... You had requested the photos via WhatsApp through their questionnaire.

In my case, after they sent me a "diagnosis" (in quotes), I called them so they could confirm that "I'm not eligible due to diffuse alopecia" and that I didn't even need to come in for an in-person consultation because "they could see it clearly from the photos." But the best part came when I asked what medical alternatives I had after explaining my history: the brilliant solution offered by one of the "supposedly" leading clinics in Valencia was to suggest I get a hair prosthesis. In other words, there are options. Welcome to the cutting edge of trichology.

It's ironic to see cases in their own website gallery with donor areas far worse than mine. But of course, the conclusion I've drawn after that call is very simple: if your case doesn't fit their "before and after" catalog with a 100% guaranteed success rate, they unilaterally decide that "you won't be happy" and send you packing without batting an eye.
I find this appalling and completely insensitive. It's not about trying to help you because you're going bald: if you're not suitable according to their criteria, you're out, because they're the ones who decide whether you'll be happy or not. Not a single contact with the doctor, not a single actual consultation... It's shameful that they try to make a profit by treating people this way.

Luckily, I didn't limit myself to just one or two options, and other clinics have (at least) had the rigor and professionalism to dedicate time to a clinical examination, explaining real medical treatments and letting me make the decision. And yes, to be perfectly honest, if you're looking for scientific rigor, empathy, or for a doctor to actually examine your head before giving up hope, look elsewhere. And yes, I expect the typical response with a lot of politically correct rhetoric to try and save face. I'm sorry, but they've already messed up. It doesn't frustrate me at all because, as I've already said, there are many other clinics in Spain that provide good assessments and diagnoses. What I received from Clínica Freitas isn't a diagnosis; it's an assessment lacking any professional rigor, deficient, and improvised.

BURNED AND SCARRED

Two years ago, I wrote a review explaining how wonderful I felt thanks to the kindness of the staff and the excellent service. That's why I've been going to them ever since for my full-body hair removal. However, about a month ago, I had my usual appointment, during which I suffered a burn that has now become a scar. At the time, I contacted them to explain the situation, and they told me to buy a cream and apply it. They gave me a brief follow-up via WhatsApp, and I waited a week hoping they would at least offer some kind of discount to compensate for the damage and discomfort I experienced. But only after a week, when I requested a complaint form, did they agree to schedule an in-person meeting. I expressed my concerns via WhatsApp, but they still told me, "The important thing for us is that you're okay; we'll see about discounts later..." Some time after requesting my complaint form, I received an email stating something like I was aware that injuries could occur with this type of service and that I had signed an agreement. Now, my question is this: is it normal that if I go to a hair removal center to improve my appearance, I get burned and left with a scar? I'm only leaving this comment so that future visitors will ask questions before signing and be aware of my experience, which might help them.

THE PAIN AND THE SCAR WILL BE A SOUVENIR.

one_star_reviews.text: I think I've been ripped off. It's the first time; I've been going for 3 or 4 years, and they did the same thing to me last year with a doctor I saw in July for two vials of hyaluronic acid. The doctor left some product for a touch-up. In September, when I went back, the doctor told me I didn't need any more, that I was fine, and on top of that, they tried to sell me other treatments. I asked the doctor how much was left over, and she said it was very little, but they didn't give me a discount. I paid whatever it was, no matter how little. It's a scam.

I'm giving them fewer stars because I can't; they are complete scammers. After spending €13,000, they tell me the operation has to be different from the one I've already paid for, offering another one that costs an additional €4,000, which I'm not interested in, since I paid for a different operation and they assured me from the beginning that they would perform it. But now they say it's no longer feasible for them. After speaking with the director more than two months ago about a possible solution, they don't answer the phone or reply to emails. It's a shame that they dedicate themselves to scamming and robbing people. They are shameless.

I had an appointment at 5:15 PM, and at 5:45 PM I decided to leave the clinic because when I asked, they told me it wouldn't be long. The issue is this: when I booked the appointments, they were only giving them out every 15 minutes. This is a private clinic, so it's unacceptable to keep you waiting for 30 minutes without any regard for your time. We can't complain about doctors in the public healthcare system, but in private clinics, they can't make you wait so long. They shouldn't be offering so many appointments if they can't keep up with the demand.

Our experience with this center has not been satisfactory.

Upon reviewing the report we received, we found errors that needed correcting, including the date the evaluation was conducted and values ​​that, for the same concept, appeared with different amounts on different pages. Taking advantage of this error correction, we requested the removal of the section containing private family information, as the report was going to be submitted to the school.

In the first correction, this request was not fully implemented, as information about our daughter's behavior at home remained. When we pointed this out, we were rather abruptly informed that a further change would cost €100. Furthermore, we found it particularly disconcerting that we were told no further changes could be made at our request, while at the same time being offered the option to make the requested change upon payment of those €100.

I was especially disappointed by the way our respectful request was handled and by the tone of the response we received.

I recommend that other parents carefully review the report as soon as they receive it, especially if they need a document for the school. It's clear to us that the school needs to know the section related to the cognitive and educational assessment, but it doesn't need to know personal aspects or details of family dynamics that belong to the private sphere.

RESPONSE TO THE OWNER - October 8, 2026

Thank you for your response, Carmen. Your reply confirms the reason for my review.

At no point did I question the assessment results or try to modify them arbitrarily. My request was to differentiate between the private information about situations that occur only within the family, which I, as a mother, provided during the evaluation, and the results of the cognitive assessment that should appear in a report for the school, so that the school could make the appropriate curricular adjustments, if deemed necessary.

I find it inappropriate to label a request related to a minor's privacy as a "parental whim." I believe families have the right to discuss what private information about their children should be included in a document that will be given to third parties, without this implying any questioning of the professional work done.

I also find it difficult to reconcile your statement that these changes "are not appropriate" with the fact that you suggested they could be included if I paid €100 for a new review of the report.

I've attached a screenshot of the email I sent with my request, so there's a record of what I actually stated. The email was sent the day after the assessment. When the assessment was completed, the report was given to me in person. Since it was a multi-page document, I thought it best to review it carefully later, rather than reading it immediately at the school.

I sincerely regret that we don't share the same viewpoint regarding the information I consider appropriate to include in a giftedness assessment report for the school.

Honestly, I was expecting a massage parlor with an elegant and upscale image, but the impression upon arrival was completely different.
The place is quite hidden, on a street that personally gave me a very bad impression. From the outside, it's practically impossible to tell what kind of establishment it is; I didn't see a clear sign, an identifiable facade, or a presentation that inspires confidence.
Since I didn't know what to expect and the first impression didn't inspire confidence, I decided not to go in and left.
For this reason, I can't comment on the interior or the service, but from the point of view of image, location, and presentation, it fell far short of what I expected from a place that promotes itself as a high-end establishment. Everything was very unpleasant.
The masseuse had told me she would see me on Sunday as well and gave me an appointment. I went, but it was closed.
⭐️ A disappointing experience. The service was very unprofessional and the attention left much to be desired.

one_star_reviews.text:
Edited review in response to IVF:
You know perfectly well that either you concealed a diagnosis or there is enormous incompetence on your part. And if it were up to me, I would report what happened so that it could be investigated whether we received adequate medical care.

We went to this clinic full of hope and trusting in what it conveys and sells: a specialized clinic, with experience in fertility problems and pathologies such as endometriosis, and with supposedly personalized and attentive care.
Today, with hindsight and, thankfully, with a happy ending, I can say that our experience was quite the opposite.
I underwent two ovarian stimulations. Between the two, we paid around €13,000 for treatment, in addition to medication (€2,000), and we obtained several embryos. After PGD, only four embryos remained, and none were viable.
The result was devastating, but the most serious thing for me is not that a fertility treatment can fail. We understand that perfectly. What I can't accept is that throughout the entire process, no one bothered to investigate what was happening.

I explained to my doctor numerous times that I was experiencing pain and various symptoms. I insisted. I mentioned it repeatedly. And no one did anything. None of the gynecologists who saw me were able to detect that I had severe endometriosis.

After we were told that we didn't have a single viable embryo, we decided to seek a second opinion. And it wasn't at another fertility clinic. It was a gynecologist completely unfamiliar with this process who listened to my symptoms, studied my case, and finally diagnosed me with severe endometriosis. With this diagnosis, it's highly unlikely that I'll have viable eggs.
He performed surgery, and after the operation, I became pregnant naturally, at over 40 years old.

Today I have a healthy and beautiful son.

And this is what makes it even harder for me, with hindsight, to accept what happened. After two stimulation sessions, thousands of euros spent, and after being made to feel that my case was due to my age, it turns out there was an underlying condition that no one wanted to see. I imagine they're instructed to stimulate and retrieve eggs, which is what's profitable, without any consideration for studying your case and making a proper diagnosis to truly help you. I wonder where the medical ethics and morals of these people stand in all this.

I'm not saying that a fertility clinic can guarantee a pregnancy. Obviously not. I'm saying something much more basic: that I expect them to properly examine the patient in front of them when she's been saying for months that something isn't right.

And a special mention for Alba because I believe her role with us deserves to be acknowledged. Alba is charming when you first meet her. She welcomes you, listens to you, inspires confidence, and knows exactly how to make you feel you've come to the right place. She charms you. She makes you feel that you'll be supported, that your case matters, and that you'll receive close follow-up.

But once you enter the process, the reality is very different.

During our treatment, that support disappeared. And when they told us that, after the entire process, there wasn't a single viable embryo, we received nothing from her, not even a simple email. In fact, I had to be the one to write to her to tell her that I hadn't received the attention we'd been promised at all.

To convince you and attract the patient, everything is about ease, kindness, and approachability. Then, when the problems start, that approachability vanishes.

And I find that especially serious in a fertility process, where we're talking about emotionally vulnerable people and very significant sums of money.
As a patient, the result is the same: no one looked for the underlying cause.
We feel deeply disappointed and cheated, both in terms of our expectations and our finances. Not because we expected a guaranteed pregnancy, but because we trusted that they would study our case, listen to our symptoms, and offer us truly personalized care. You don't deserve what you charge.

Hello! My experience with the recession clinics was phenomenal, very kind and attentive! However, there's an issue regarding my refund. Ten months ago, in December 2025, I paid €3,500. I didn't see a surgeon or anything. I handed over my money because they told me that if I couldn't have breast augmentation surgery, they would refund me within 15 days. To this day, I haven't received my money back. I received an email from Dorsia saying they had already processed the refund, but I'm still waiting. Every week, they told me to keep an eye on my account, and nothing! I've filed another claim and am still waiting for a response. I need my money back; I worked very hard for it, and I couldn't have the surgery due to health reasons.

If they don't resolve this this month, I will take further action.

My experience with this clinic has been very negative. The customer service leaves much to be desired: they don't answer calls, and after paying for a weight loss plan, a week has passed and I still haven't received the appropriate attention. What surprised me most is that, instead of offering a solution, a clinic employee contacted me to reprimand me for contacting the clinic via WhatsApp with questions about my own plan. I believe that, once payment has been made, the least I can expect is proper attention and the opportunity to have my questions about the contracted service answered. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
It's best not to risk it with this store. Everything is perfect until a problem arises... If something goes wrong, forget it. They stop being a good store if they refuse to take responsibility for their mistakes. Then you wish you'd worked with Ikea kitchens, which offer much, much more for less.
Let me tell you... We had our kitchen designed by them, and we bought several appliances, but we already had the induction cooktop for a year in our old kitchen without any problems. The salesperson and the designer asked us for the model of the cooktop, and surprise, surprise, when they installed it, it overheated terribly. We reported it, and they cut the back of the cabinet and lowered the cutlery drawer... The installer said that this design is problematic because it lacks ventilation... The problems continued; the cooktop would go into safety mode and reduce the power mid-cooking. We kept reporting it, and finally, it broke.

We reported it, and after almost a month without a cooktop (it was August!), they washed their hands of it, saying they couldn't provide written confirmation that the kitchen ventilation was adequate. They told us to buy another cooktop, but if the same thing happens, they won't be responsible.

Conclusion: I wouldn't risk it because their after-sales service is appalling. There are many other places that will give you better service and more peace of mind. Luckily, we warned our friends and now you all... The photo shows how we're cooking now.

one_star_reviews.text:
I received terrible service from Orvecame, located on Calle Escaleras in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria.

Therefore, it doesn't deserve even one star, which I had to give in order to submit this review.
It concerns a rental car, a 2016 Lancia Ypsilon semi-automatic, for which an appointment was scheduled in mid-July 2026. However, no appointment was available to diagnose the problem before August 18, 2026, at 10:30 AM.
We accepted the appointment, providing the vehicle's information, such as the license plate number, and stating that it had been previously inspected at another workshop, where they were unable to determine the problem. We were advised to take it to the authorized dealership.

The vehicle malfunctioned: it stalled while driving on the highway and would not restart.

Last Monday, the day of the appointment, we had the vehicle towed to the aforementioned workshop.

When the tow truck arrived at the garage, they informed the driver, before even unloading the car, that they were refusing to accept it, saying it was "an old car" and they wouldn't service it.

Furthermore, when we spoke directly with the garage manager, she repeated the reason for not accepting the vehicle. I asked her to give me a written explanation, but she said she didn't provide anything in writing, only over the phone. When I told her that they would have to pay for the towing, she said she wasn't responsible for anything and that complaints should be handled through the "customer service" department.
That's why I'm sharing this review: Be careful with this company when scheduling an appointment for an "old" vehicle. They could have informed me before I wasted this valuable time, during which the vehicle couldn't be rented, in addition to the towing costs.

one_star_reviews.text:
THIS REVIEW IS FOR MOVETOMADRID/ELIANA EUDES
I hired Move To Madrid for relocation assistance after moving to Madrid and paid over €2,200 for their services. Unfortunately, my experience was very disappointing.

One example was a rental company I was particularly interested in. The agent told me that the company was “snobby” and strongly discouraged me from working with them. Despite this, I remained very interested in their apartments. The agent then told me that she would personally go to their offices, introduce herself, and view their apartments so that she could help me determine whether they would be a good option. I relied on her representation that she would do this.

She later backed away from that commitment and told me that the company did not allow apartment viewings. I subsequently learned that this was not accurate and that viewings were in fact possible. This was extremely frustrating because I was paying for professional relocation assistance specifically so that I could have informed access to the Madrid rental market, yet I felt that I was being discouraged from pursuing an option I had independently identified and was genuinely interested in.

One particularly frustrating example involved getting a Spanish bank account and Spanish phone number. The agent insisted that I needed to open a Spanish bank account before I could obtain a Spanish phone number. However, the bank itself required a Spanish phone number as part of the process. This put me in a circular situation where I could not complete either step. The agent accompanied me to the bank, but the appointment was unsuccessful, and both she and the bank employee asked me for a “TNI” number that does not apply to me. I was ultimately able to find an alternative solution and arrange these things myself. Her guidance was confusing and, based on what the bank actually required, objectively incorrect, and it actively prevented me from completing the process.

There were also issues regarding additional charges. The Padrón appointment was included in our services, and when we specifically asked whether there would be an additional charge for the agent to attend, we were told in writing that there would not be one. We were subsequently asked to pay for the agent’s train tickets from her vacation destination in order for her to attend the appointment.

I also paid an additional €200 for legal assistance with appointments. My husband handled his appointment himself, and €100 was refunded. The remaining €100 was not refunded even though the lawyer was never used. I never authorized that €100 to be converted into payment to the agent for another service.

The agent later assisted me with my DNI appointment, but this was not something I had agreed would replace the unused €100 of legal assistance. She subsequently used this assistance as a reason why she believed she was entitled to retain the €100, including telling me that she had been to the police station four times on my behalf. To be clear, I never requested that she make those four trips, and despite doing so, she still provided me with incorrect information regarding the DNI process. I did not agree to pay €100 for this assistance, nor did I agree that it would substitute for the legal service that I had originally paid for.

We also never received invoices for the payments we made.

Beyond the service issues, I found the agent’s conduct and comments extremely unprofessional. On multiple occasions, she referred to female employees at the bank and at Homeclub as “stupid” and said that men were better to work with. She also told me that she preferred to work only with “rich, good-looking clients.” I found these comments particularly inappropriate in a professional setting. She said more inappropriate things directly to me about my appearance and the fact I looked terrible in photos/don't look Spanish.

There is also another Google review on the Move To Madrid listing describing a similar experience involving Eliana. I encourage prospective clients to find that review on Google Maps and read it as well.

I went to this clinic on Monday, and the experience was terrible.

I expected a consultation for moles or warts to include a check-up of all of them, along with a brief interview. I was there for ten minutes, if that. They removed the wart, but it hurt because the first injection of anesthetic wasn't enough, and I felt a burning sensation, so they injected me again.
They didn't check any other moles. The service was curt, lacking empathy, and they were clearly eager to finish.
At reception, they charged me €310 for removing a small wart, and they didn't provide an itemized bill, receipt, or any other kind of payment.
And to top it all off, they supposedly planned to send it for analysis, even though they told me it wasn't dangerous and that if they didn't notify me, I should call them myself.
I understand that it's a reputable clinic, but that doesn't justify exorbitant prices. If they do have high prices, the service should be professional, humane, and efficient. I absolutely do not recommend it.
