one_star_reviews.text:
They came to my house because my air conditioner stopped working. The guys from Endesa came and told me that fixing it would cost over €600 and that I should just get a new one. They asked if I wanted a quote, and the first quote already included an extra €100. I asked them about it, and they said they'd made a mistake. So far, so good.

A few days later, while I was thinking about replacing it, I found out a friend who installs air conditioners. He asked me if I'd replaced the capacitor, which only costs €9, to rule it out. I said no, because the technician who came said it was the compressor. He said, "Let's replace it just to try it," and eureka! Now it works. It only took us 5 minutes, and for €9, it's fixed.
I've been stuck with it through the hottest days because they wouldn't replace it to test it.

I think that sometimes it's worth wasting a little time, even if I have to come back another day to fix it, since I probably shouldn't have even had to pay for the part because I have a maintenance plan and I think it covers the labor for the repair and some parts.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would like to report a recent incident: there was no sign posted where my water bottle fell, even though it was clearly an accident and not intentional. Despite this, the staff implied that we were entirely at fault.

I would like to point out that the water bottle only sustained a minor impact—a fall of less than 20 cm—and was already dented before the impact. Furthermore, no paint chipped as a result of the fall, strongly suggesting that the damage was already present. This made us feel trapped in the situation.

If such a minor impact is (supposedly) enough to damage the product, it seriously raises questions about the value for money of this item.

I also regret having to point out a shocking lack of courtesy and politeness on the part of the staff: not a single hello or goodbye during our entire visit. The only time they spoke to us was to accuse us and make us pay.

I would have appreciated a little more understanding and professionalism from the staff in handling this situation.

I strongly advise against going there.

one_star_reviews.text:
COMPLAINT
Today I called the health center to request a medical evaluation. I explained over the phone that I didn't consider it an emergency, but that I needed to be evaluated due to certain symptoms related to circulatory problems and my general health.
The center informed me that, at most, they could offer me an urgent appointment for that same day, so I went at the indicated time.
During the consultation, when I began to explain the reasons why I had requested the evaluation, the professional told me that this type of appointment was for urgent cases and that I should be seen by my regular doctor. I was not allowed to calmly explain the set of symptoms and medical history that had led me to request the evaluation.

Ultimately, only a very limited evaluation was performed, and I was told that I would have blood work done.

My complaint is not because I believe a specific test should be performed, but because I feel I was not given the opportunity to adequately explain the reason for my visit, nor was I offered sufficiently attentive care, especially considering that the center itself instructed me to come for that type of appointment.

I request a review of what happened and, in particular, the procedure by which these types of appointments are being managed, as I find it contradictory that I was offered an urgent appointment after explaining my situation and then, once there, was criticized for having come for that type of appointment without even having had the opportunity to properly explain the problem.

I also request that the importance of allowing patients to explain their symptoms before determining whether or not the appointment falls under the urgent care service be taken into account.

ANTAD Puerto de la Cruz
I went today on my doctor's recommendation. Initially, I entered the lab by mistake; a very kind employee gave me directions with interest and diligence to get to the social services center and resolve my issue.
Upon entering the center, I found the doors locked and heard people inside. When I knocked, they asked me several times who I was and what I wanted. When they finally opened the door, they told me to go to other centers in the area, asked who told me to come, and asked if the appointment there would be delayed, etc. The problem is that these questions were asked in an unpleasant tone, as it seemed they were more interested in chatting with their colleagues than attending to the needs of a user of the Canary Islands Health Service (SCS). I feel sorry for the teenager who might come after me with a problem they aren't interested in solving while they have their coffee on the table. I was seen by Montse, a "social worker." In this case, she didn't fulfill her role.
The service is awful... nonexistent professionalism... it's better to take your own life than come to this place for help.
